1Summary

Automated checks found nothing that blocks interpretation. Results are ready for scientific review.

21,195 of 46,427 genes passed the expression filter and were tested across 33 samples for the contrast tnt_response: responder vs non_responder. At an adjusted p-value threshold of 0.05, 3 genes were differentially expressed (2 up, 1 down).

The strongest increases were PURPL, LRRN1, and the strongest decreases GSDMA.

Pathway analysis of the ranked gene list recovered Hallmark E2F Targets (NES +2.81), Gobp Cellular Defense Response (NES +2.76), Gobp Glial Cell Activation (NES +2.75), Hallmark G2M Checkpoint (NES +2.72) (FDR < 0.25).

5Pathway enrichment

5014 gene sets were tested against the ranked gene list; 733 reached FDR < 0.25.

Each bar is its own test, and its length is the result rather than a count of anything. The normalised enrichment score asks how far towards one end of the ranked gene list a set's members sit, and divides by what sets of that size reach on permuted data — so a 20-gene set and a 200-gene one can be put side by side. The sign is the direction: positive means higher in the treatment group.

Bars at full strength passed FDR 0.25 and carry their value; faded bars were tested and did not. The figure shows the strongest 14 of the 5642 sets that had enough measured genes to test.

6Pathway network

Pathways that share genes are drawn together, so a block of linked terms is usually one signal seen several ways rather than several independent findings.

Enrichment map

Each node is an enriched gene set; a link means the two share at least a quarter of the smaller set's genes (the overlap coefficient EnrichmentMap uses, which keeps a small set nested inside a large one connected). Red is induced, blue repressed, node size is |NES|, and the ring is the posterior that the term is real. Drag a node, hover for detail, raise the slider to keep only the tightest gene sharing.

9Literature context

Every hit was counted against Europe PMC: how often it appears alongside this experiment's context, against how often it would by chance given how much the gene is studied at all. That denominator is what separates a specific finding from a famous gene — without it a loading control outranks a real one.

0 of the tested hits are already established here; 0 are studied elsewhere but have no literature in this context, which is where a follow-up would start.

10Methods

Raw counts were filtered to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 33 samples. Library size differences were corrected with median-of-ratios size factors. Gene-wise negative-binomial dispersions were estimated by Cox-Reid adjusted profile likelihood, fitted to a parametric mean-dispersion trend (alpha = a0 + a1/mu) and shrunk toward that trend by empirical Bayes. A negative-binomial generalised linear model with a log link and the design Intercept + tnt_response[responder] + sex[male] + age was fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares, and the coefficient of interest was tested with a Wald statistic referred to a t distribution whose degrees of freedom combine the residual degrees of freedom with the prior degrees of freedom implied by the dispersion shrinkage. Genes whose fit was dominated by a single sample (Cook's distance above the 99th percentile of F(4, 29)) were set aside. P-values were adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure after independent filtering on mean expression. Log2 fold changes reported for ranking were shrunk under a normal prior whose variance was estimated from the observed spread of the estimates.

Analyses were run on BioFlow AI; the run manifest records every package version, parameter and input file hash needed to reproduce them.

Genes were ranked by the Wald statistic of the contrast. Pre-ranked gene set enrichment analysis was run with a weighted Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic (weight = 1.0) and 1000 gene-label permutations per set; enrichment scores were normalised by the mean absolute score of same-sign permutations and the resulting p-values adjusted by Benjamini-Hochberg. Leading-edge genes are those contributing to the running statistic up to its extremum.

Gene sets: MSigDB v2025.1 Hallmark + GO:BP. Gene sets: MSigDB v2025.1 (Hallmark and GO Biological Process), Broad Institute and UC San Diego, used under CC BY 4.0. Liberzon et al., Cell Systems 2015; Subramanian et al., PNAS 2005. Sets were restricted to those with between 8 and 500 measured genes; figures and the narrative show the strongest sets after removing those whose leading edge repeats one already shown (Jaccard > 0.6), while the tables carry every set tested.
